atoms.text: This guide configures a bucket to receive request logs from Gatewaylog, a load-balancing service, for gateways in account 111122223333. Create a bucket named example-gateway-logs in the same Region as the gateways and keep Block Public Access enabled. Gatewaylog writes one compressed log object every five minutes under the prefix gateway/AWSLogs/111122223333/. Add a bucket policy statement with Effect set to Allow, Action set to s3:PutObject, and Principal set to the AWS account ID 222233334444, which is the regional log-writer account Gatewaylog uses in your Region. Set Resource to arn:aws:s3:::example-gateway-logs/gateway/AWSLogs/111122223333/* so that writes are limited to that prefix. Do not grant s3:GetObject or s3:ListBucket to this principal, because delivery requires write access only. Save the policy, then enable access logging on the gateway and specify the bucket name and the prefix gateway. Gatewaylog writes a test object when logging is enabled, and the enable call fails with an access error if the write is denied.

This guide configures a bucket to receive request logs from Gatewaylog, a load-balancing service, for gateways in account 111122223333. Create a bucket named example-gateway-logs in the same Region as the gateways and keep Block Public Access enabled. Gatewaylog writes one compressed log object every five minutes under the prefix gateway/AWSLogs/111122223333/. Add a bucket policy statement with Effect set to Allow, Action set to s3:PutObject, and Principal set to the service principal gatewaylog.amazonaws.com. Set Resource to arn:aws:s3:::example-gateway-logs/gateway/AWSLogs/111122223333/* and add a StringEquals condition on aws:SourceAccount with the value 111122223333, so that only your gateways can cause writes to that prefix. Do not grant s3:GetObject or s3:ListBucket to this principal, because delivery requires write access only. Save the policy, then enable access logging on the gateway and specify the bucket name and the prefix gateway. Gatewaylog writes a test object when logging is enabled, and the enable call fails with an access error if the write is denied.

This guide describes the bucket policy for storing audit events produced by Trailkeeper, an account activity recording service. Trailkeeper delivers a JSON file of events roughly every five minutes to the prefix trail/AWSLogs/444455556666/ in the bucket example-audit-archive. Before the first delivery, Trailkeeper checks that it can read the bucket ACL, so the policy needs two statements. The first statement allows s3:GetBucketAcl on arn:aws:s3:::example-audit-archive for the IAM role arn:aws:iam::444455556666:role/TrailkeeperDeliveryRole. The second statement allows s3:PutObject on arn:aws:s3:::example-audit-archive/trail/AWSLogs/444455556666/* for the same role, with a StringEquals condition requiring s3:x-amz-acl to be bucket-owner-full-control. Create the role with a trust policy that lets Trailkeeper assume it in your account, and attach no other permissions to it. After saving the policy, create the trail and point it at the bucket and the prefix trail. If the first statement is missing, trail creation fails with an error stating that the bucket ACL cannot be read.

Trailkeeper delivers a JSON file of events roughly every five minutes to the prefix trail/AWSLogs/444455556666/ in the bucket example-audit-archive. Before the first delivery, Trailkeeper checks that it can read the bucket ACL, so the policy needs two statements. The first statement allows s3:GetBucketAcl on arn:aws:s3:::example-audit-archive for the service principal trailkeeper.amazonaws.com. The second statement allows s3:PutObject on arn:aws:s3:::example-audit-archive/trail/AWSLogs/444455556666/* for the same service principal, with a StringEquals condition requiring s3:x-amz-acl to be bucket-owner-full-control. Add an aws:SourceArn condition of arn:aws:trailkeeper:us-east-1:444455556666:trail/main-trail to both statements so that only that trail can use them. After saving the policy, create the trail and point it at the bucket and the prefix trail. If the first statement is missing, trail creation fails with an error stating that the bucket ACL cannot be read.

This guide covers delivery of network flow records from Flowtrace, a traffic monitoring service, to a bucket in the account 777788889999. Flowtrace writes records in Parquet format, partitioned by year, month, day, and hour, under the prefix flow/. Create the bucket example-flow-records and set object ownership to bucket owner enforced, so that all delivered objects belong to your account. Add a statement with Effect set to Allow, Action set to s3:PutObject, and Principal set to the IAM role arn:aws:iam::777788889999:role/FlowtraceWriterRole. Limit Resource to arn:aws:s3:::example-flow-records/flow/* and add a second action, s3:GetBucketLocation, scoped to the bucket ARN itself. The role is the identity that Flowtrace assumes when it writes, so its trust policy must name the Flowtrace delivery configuration in your account. Create the flow log subscription for each virtual network and reference the bucket ARN with the prefix flow. Records for each hour appear in the matching partition within about ten minutes after the hour closes.

This guide covers delivery of network flow records from Flowtrace, a traffic monitoring service, to a bucket in the account 777788889999. Flowtrace writes records in Parquet format, partitioned by year, month, day, and hour, under the prefix flow/. Create the bucket example-flow-records and set object ownership to bucket owner enforced, so that all delivered objects belong to your account. Add a statement with Effect set to Allow, Action set to s3:PutObject, and Principal set to the service principal flowtrace.amazonaws.com. Limit Resource to arn:aws:s3:::example-flow-records/flow/* and add a second action, s3:GetBucketLocation, scoped to the bucket ARN itself. Add conditions that require aws:SourceAccount to equal 777788889999 and aws:SourceArn to match arn:aws:flowtrace:us-east-1:777788889999:subscription/*. Create the flow log subscription for each virtual network and reference the bucket ARN with the prefix flow. Records for each hour appear in the matching partition within about ten minutes after the hour closes.

This guide explains how to receive standard delivery logs from Edgelog, a content distribution service, in the bucket example-edge-logs. Edgelog writes gzip-compressed files, each covering a few minutes of viewer requests, to the prefix edge/E1A2B3C4/. The bucket must grant write access to the AWS account ID 888899990000, which is the account Edgelog uses for log delivery. Add a statement with Effect set to Allow, Action set to s3:PutObject, and Principal set to arn:aws:iam::888899990000:root, with Resource set to arn:aws:s3:::example-edge-logs/edge/*. Add a separate statement allowing s3:GetBucketAcl and s3:PutBucketAcl on the bucket ARN to the same account, because Edgelog reads and updates the bucket ACL when logging is activated. Do not apply a lifecycle rule to the prefix until you confirm that downstream readers have copied the files. Enable standard logging on the distribution and enter the bucket and the prefix edge. Files first appear within an hour, and a missing file after that period usually indicates a policy mismatch.

This guide explains how to receive standard delivery logs from Edgelog, a content distribution service, in the bucket example-edge-logs. Edgelog writes gzip-compressed files, each covering a few minutes of viewer requests, to the prefix edge/E1A2B3C4/. The bucket must grant write access to the Edgelog service principal, edgelog.amazonaws.com. Add a statement with Effect set to Allow, Action set to s3:PutObject, and Principal set to the service principal, with Resource set to arn:aws:s3:::example-edge-logs/edge/* and a condition that aws:SourceArn equals the ARN of your distribution. Add a separate statement allowing s3:GetBucketAcl and s3:PutBucketAcl on the bucket ARN to the same service principal, because Edgelog reads and updates the bucket ACL when logging is activated. Do not apply a lifecycle rule to the prefix until you confirm that downstream readers have copied the files. Enable standard logging on the distribution and enter the bucket and the prefix edge. Files first appear within an hour, and a missing file after that period usually indicates a policy mismatch.

This guide sets up a central bucket for server access logs, where the logging source is a set of application buckets owned by account 123456789012. The target bucket is example-central-access-logs, and each source bucket writes objects whose keys begin with the source bucket name and a slash. Create a bucket policy statement with Effect set to Allow and Action set to s3:PutObject. Set Principal to the IAM role arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/AccessLogDeliveryRole, which the logging feature uses to write on behalf of the source buckets. Set Resource to arn:aws:s3:::example-central-access-logs/* and add a StringEquals condition on aws:PrincipalAccount with the value 123456789012. The target bucket must be in the same Region as the source buckets, and it must not have a default retention lock that blocks delivery. Enable server access logging on each source bucket and choose the target bucket with a prefix such as app-a/. Log records are delivered on a best-effort basis, usually within a few hours of the requests they describe.

This guide sets up a central bucket for server access logs, where the logging source is a set of application buckets owned by account 123456789012. The target bucket is example-central-access-logs, and each source bucket writes objects whose keys begin with the source bucket name and a slash. Create a bucket policy statement with Effect set to Allow and Action set to s3:PutObject. Set Principal to the service principal logging.s3.amazonaws.com, which the logging feature uses to write on behalf of the source buckets. Set Resource to arn:aws:s3:::example-central-access-logs/* and add a StringEquals condition on aws:SourceAccount with the value 123456789012 and an ArnLike condition on aws:SourceArn with the value arn:aws:s3:::app-*. The target bucket must be in the same Region as the source buckets, and it must not have a default retention lock that blocks delivery. Enable server access logging on each source bucket and choose the target bucket with a prefix such as app-a/. Log records are delivered on a best-effort basis, usually within a few hours of the requests they describe.

This guide configures storage of DNS query logs generated by Resolvewatch, a managed name resolution service, in the bucket example-dns-query-logs. Resolvewatch emits one file per resolver endpoint every ten minutes and writes it under the prefix dns/endpoint-id/. Create the bucket in account 555566667777 and enable default encryption with an object-store-managed key. Add a bucket policy statement allowing s3:PutObject on arn:aws:s3:::example-dns-query-logs/dns/* with Principal set to the IAM user arn:aws:iam::555566667777:user/resolvewatch-log-writer. The delivery configuration stores that user's credentials, so rotate its access key on a schedule and avoid attaching permissions beyond this statement. Add a second statement allowing s3:ListBucket on the bucket ARN to the same user, restricted by an s3:prefix condition of dns/*. Create the query log configuration, attach it to the resolver endpoints, and set the destination to the bucket ARN. Check the prefix after twenty minutes; the first files should be present.

This guide configures storage of DNS query logs generated by Resolvewatch, a managed name resolution service, in the bucket example-dns-query-logs. Resolvewatch emits one file per resolver endpoint every ten minutes and writes it under the prefix dns/endpoint-id/. Create the bucket in account 555566667777 and enable default encryption with an object-store-managed key. Add a bucket policy statement allowing s3:PutObject on arn:aws:s3:::example-dns-query-logs/dns/* with Principal set to the service principal resolvewatch.amazonaws.com. The delivery configuration needs no stored credentials, so the statement itself should carry an aws:SourceAccount condition of 555566667777 and an aws:SourceArn condition matching the query log configuration. Add a second statement allowing s3:ListBucket on the bucket ARN to the same service principal, restricted by an s3:prefix condition of dns/*. Create the query log configuration, attach it to the resolver endpoints, and set the destination to the bucket ARN. Check the prefix after twenty minutes; the first files should be present.

This guide describes how to export database audit logs from Tablegrid, a managed relational database service, to the bucket example-db-audit-exports. Tablegrid uploads one file per instance every fifteen minutes under the prefix tablegrid/instance-name/, and the files are encrypted with a customer-managed key. The bucket policy statement allows s3:PutObject and s3:AbortMultipartUpload on arn:aws:s3:::example-db-audit-exports/tablegrid/*. Set Principal to the IAM role arn:aws:iam::999900001111:role/TablegridExportRole, and add a condition requiring s3:x-amz-server-side-encryption to equal aws:kms. Grant the role use of the encryption key in the key policy, since the bucket policy alone does not permit key operations. Larger audit files are uploaded as multipart uploads, which is why the abort action is included. Enable audit log export on each instance and select the bucket and the prefix tablegrid. Confirm delivery by listing the prefix after the first interval and checking that the object size is greater than zero.

Set Principal to the service principal tablegrid.amazonaws.com, and add a condition requiring s3:x-amz-server-side-encryption to equal aws:kms, together with an aws:SourceAccount condition of 999900001111. Grant the service use of the encryption key in the key policy, since the bucket policy alone does not permit key operations. Larger audit files are uploaded as multipart uploads, which is why the abort action is included. Enable audit log export on each instance and select the bucket and the prefix tablegrid. Confirm delivery by listing the prefix after the first interval and checking that the object size is greater than zero.

This guide sets up a centralized bucket in a security account, 121212121212, that collects firewall logs from Shieldwall, a network protection service, running in member accounts. The bucket is named example-central-firewall-logs, and Shieldwall writes files under the prefix shieldwall/member-account-id/. Add a statement with Effect set to Allow and Action set to s3:PutObject. Set Principal to the IAM role arn:aws:iam::333344445555:role/ShieldwallLogRole, which is deployed in each member account and uses the same role name. Because the member accounts differ, list their role ARNs as an array under Principal, or use a wildcard principal with an aws:PrincipalOrgID condition for your organization. Set Resource to arn:aws:s3:::example-central-firewall-logs/shieldwall/*. Add a statement allowing s3:GetBucketAcl on the bucket ARN to the same principals so that Shieldwall can validate the destination. Configure each member account's firewall to deliver to the bucket ARN, then verify that a prefix exists for each account ID.

This guide sets up a centralized bucket in a security account, 121212121212, that collects firewall logs from Shieldwall, a network protection service, running in member accounts. The bucket is named example-central-firewall-logs, and Shieldwall writes files under the prefix shieldwall/member-account-id/. Add a statement with Effect set to Allow and Action set to s3:PutObject. Set Principal to the service principal shieldwall.amazonaws.com, which delivers on behalf of every member account. Because the member accounts differ, restrict the statement with an aws:SourceOrgID condition for your organization, or list the accounts under an aws:SourceAccount condition as an array. Set Resource to arn:aws:s3:::example-central-firewall-logs/shieldwall/*. Add a statement allowing s3:GetBucketAcl on the bucket ARN to the same service principal so that Shieldwall can validate the destination. Configure each member account's firewall to deliver to the bucket ARN, then verify that a prefix exists for each account ID.
